clue.text: Saint Jude's initial hopes dashed

indicators.note: the initial of a name is its opening letter, so only the start of Jude's is taken
hopes that are dashed are smashed, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A saint called Jude is downcast because his hopes have come to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initial' takes J from Jude's; 'dashed' rearranges J plus HOPES. Jude is a saint too, which makes 'Saint Jude' look like one unit, but 'Saint' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph, husband of Mary, is venerated as a saint in the Christian calendar.

clue.text: Jack meets a pleasant girl

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack on playing cards
pleasant means nice

explanation.surface: A man called Jack is introduced to an agreeable young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Janice is a female given name, so it can stand for a girl in crosswords.

clue.text: A sweet term of endearment

definitions.meaning: a small round sugared confection, a piece of candy
a pet name used affectionately for a loved one, like 'honey'

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a little boiled confection and an affectionate pet name, much as 'sweetie' does.

clue.text: Potty uncle upset composer

parts.note: a potty is a chamber pot, which is informally called a po

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters of uncle are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A crazy relative is upset about some piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potty' reads as an adjective meaning mad describing the uncle; it is a noun giving PO, a British word for a chamber pot. 'upset' rearranges UNCLE to ULENC.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Poulenc was a twentieth-century French composer, one of the group called Les Six.

clue.text: Telescope taken from agent by good young woman

parts.note: a secret agent is a spy
a lass is a young woman or girl

explanation.surface: A telescope is confiscated from a spy by a virtuous girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A spyglass is a small hand-held telescope, as carried by sailors.

clue.text: Us actress and Scottish actor supporting musician

indicators.note: in a down answer a supporting piece sits underneath, so it comes after the other one

parts.note: a piper is a musician who plays the bagpipes
John Laurie was a Scottish actor, best known for Dad's Army, the British TV sitcom about the Home Guard

explanation.surface: An American actress and a Scottish actor play backing roles for a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Us' is printed for US, the United States. In a down clue 'supporting' puts LAURIE beneath PIPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Piper Laurie is an American actress known for The Hustler and Carrie, so she is a US film star.

clue.text: Book English rock band

definitions.meaning: the opening book of the Bible
a British progressive rock group whose members included Peter Gabriel and Phil Collins

explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to the first book of the Old Testament and to the band formed at Charterhouse school in 1967.

clue.text: A second artist brought over bouquet

indicators.note: something brought over is turned around, so the whole run of pieces is read backwards in this down answer

parts.note: mo is a short informal word for a moment or second
RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Someone with a moment to spare carries an artist's flowers across.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought over' reverses the whole string A + MO + RA, giving the answer read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine's bouquet is its smell, so the word is a synonym for fragrance.

clue.text: Kind nurse, extremely lonely

parts.note: in British hospitals a sister is a senior nurse in charge of a ward

indicators.note: the extremes of the word lonely are its first and last letters, which are the only ones kept

explanation.surface: A caring nurse is terribly lonely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' looks like an intensifier for 'lonely' but takes its first and last letters, L and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisterly means kindly and affectionate, as a sibling would be to another.

clue.text: Rang up about an Indian city

indicators.note: about means around or in disorder here, so the letters of the phrase are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone telephoned about a city in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rang up' reads as phoned, but its six letters are rearranged, signalled by 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nagpur is a large city in Maharashtra, central India.

clue.text: Views nose of one-eleven and wings

indicators.note: the nose is at the front, so only the opening letter of one-eleven is used

parts.note: a pinion is a bird's wing, especially its outer part

explanation.surface: Thoughts on the nose and wings of a One-Eleven, an old British airliner.
explanation.walkthrough: The BAC One-Eleven was a British jet airliner, so 'nose' and 'wings' make aeronautical sense; the nose of 'one-eleven' is O.
explanation.definitionFit: Opinions are views in the sense of beliefs or judgments someone holds.

clue.text: Go in after fish and chips

indicators.note: after places the piece for go in behind the piece for fish

parts.note: a carp is a freshwater fish
to go in is to enter

explanation.surface: Head inside for some fish and chips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fish and chips' is the British takeaway meal, but 'chips' is the definition: Chips is a traditional nickname for a carpenter, especially a ship's carpenter.
explanation.definitionFit: Chips is the long-standing nickname of a woodworker, notably on board ship, from the wood chips such tradesmen make.

clue.text: Dealing illegally with transport supremo

parts.note: traffic is vehicles moving along roads, the business of transport
a king is a supreme ruler or supremo

explanation.surface: Illegal dealing in goods involving the head of transport.
explanation.definitionFit: Trafficking means trading illicitly, as in drugs or people.

clue.text: Reprimand son, out of office

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son, as in genealogies
late can mean former, as with a late chairman who no longer holds the post

explanation.surface: A father scolds his son, who has lost his job.
explanation.definitionFit: To slate someone is to criticise or rebuke them harshly.

clue.text: Abroad I sack a lad I mostly call careless

indicators.note: abroad here means scattered widely, so the letters of these words are dispersed and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: most of the word call is used, its final letter dropped

explanation.surface: Working overseas, a boss sacks a lad and calls him sloppy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abroad' rearranges ISACKALADI into LACKADAISI; 'mostly' cuts CALL to CAL, which ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lackadaisical describes someone lacking enthusiasm and effort, so it means careless or lazy.

clue.text: Verses clergyman shortened — he was heartless

indicators.note: shortened means cut short, so the final letter of the word for clergyman is removed

parts.note: a cleric is a clergyman

indicators.note: a heartless word loses its middle, so only the outer letters of was remain

explanation.surface: Poems about a vicar who has been cut short because he was unfeeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' looks like a description of the clergyman but takes the middle A out of WAS, giving WS.
explanation.definitionFit: Clerihews are comic four-line biographical poems, invented by Edmund Clerihew Bentley.

clue.text: Crustacean in catch caught by seaman across river

parts.note: to land a fish is to catch it

indicators.note: across means spanning, so the pieces for caught and seaman stretch either side of the river abbreviation

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A crab is caught in a net by a sailor working across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a sailor catching a crab, but 'in' is only a link; 'across' means the river letter is spanned by the caught-plus-seaman pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A land crab is a crab that lives mostly on land, still a crustacean.

clue.text: A little luck may get you a lot of money

definitions.meaning: read literally, a modest amount of good luck, fortune meaning chance
the idiom ironically means a very large sum

explanation.definitionFit: Fortune means both luck and wealth, so a modest amount of luck and the ironic idiom for a big sum share the phrase.

clue.text: European valiant at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters of valiant are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A brave sailor from the continent is out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latvian is a native of Latvia, a Baltic state, so a European.

clue.text: Defenceless cockney's alive and well

indicators.note: a cockney, a working-class Londoner, traditionally drops the H sound, so that letter goes

parts.note: someone alive and well after an incident is unharmed

explanation.surface: A Londoner without weapons is nevertheless fine and healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cockney's' signals dropping the H, as a London accent does: 'unharmed' becomes 'un'armed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Unarmed means carrying no weapons, so without means of defence.

clue.text: Nicaraguan president — in short, egalitarian

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the words short and egalitarian, running across them

explanation.surface: A Central American leader described briefly as believing in equality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in short' looks like a phrase meaning briefly; 'in' is the signal and the name runs from short into egalitarian.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Ortega led the Sandinistas and has been President of Nicaragua.

clue.text: Old coin adult found in passage

indicators.note: found in means placed within, so the abbreviation for adult goes inside the word for passage

parts.note: a duct is a tube or passage carrying air or fluid
A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up discovers an antique piece of money in a corridor.
explanation.definitionFit: The ducat was a gold or silver coin used across Europe in earlier centuries.

clue.text: Copper on border, cut up?

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a border in a garden is a flower bed

explanation.surface: Was a policeman on the edge upset?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a police officer and 'cut up' distress; the question mark flags that cut up means chopped into small pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is cubed has been chopped into small square pieces, one way of cutting it.

clue.text: Surprisingly leave rich knight

indicators.note: surprisingly signals an unexpected change, so the letters of these words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A knight unexpectedly departs a wealthy man.
explanation.definitionFit: Chevalier is the French title for a knight, used in English for members of some chivalric orders.

clue.text: Polish strike adds insult to injury

parts.note: to polish is to rub
a sit-in is a form of strike or protest occupation

explanation.surface: Workers in Poland stage a strike, making a bad situation worse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' at the start of the clue disguises the verb polish as the nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: To rub it in is to keep reminding someone of a failure, making matters worse.

clue.text: I'm deep in trouble bringing hamper

indicators.note: in trouble means in a mess, so the letters of I'm deep are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone admits being in serious difficulty after bringing a picnic basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hamper' reads as a basket but is the verb meaning to hold back.
explanation.definitionFit: To impede someone is to obstruct or hinder their progress.

clue.text: Mark engaging in a witty conversation

indicators.note: engaging means taking in or enclosing, so the word for mark wraps around in a

parts.note: a badge is a mark or emblem of identity

explanation.surface: Someone stands out by taking part in clever repartee.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is playful, teasing banter between people.

clue.text: Bubbly does it, and port

indicators.note: bubbly suggests fizzing and frothing, so the letters of does are stirred up

parts.note: taken as written
it can mean sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: Champagne does the job, and so does a fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bubbly' and 'port' both suggest drinks; port here is a harbour city, Odessa on the Black Sea in Ukraine.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is a major seaport on Ukraine's Black Sea coast.
